profile.name: Jyothi Siddalingappa Jayanna
profile.title: Platform and DevOps Engineer
profile.summary: M.Sc. Web Engineering student at TU Chemnitz with 3+ years of professional experience as a Platform and DevOps Engineer at A.P. Moller–Maersk. Experienced in Java and Spring Boot backend development, Temporal workflows, Kubernetes on Azure, and CI/CD automation. Internal platform tooling she contributed to is used by 8,000+ engineers. Immediately available for a working student role in DevOps, cloud, or backend engineering, up to 20 hours per week during the semester.

experience.role: Platform Engineer, Internal Developer Platform team
highlights: Built Java, Spring Boot, and Temporal backend workflows for deployment validation and service onboarding on an internal platform used by 8,000+ engineers.
Built a Temporal deletion workflow that removes service integrations, associated data, and Kubernetes resources.
Developed Application Catalog and GitHub integrations for service registration, repository creation, custom properties, and CI setup.
Co-maintained team synchronization across Azure, GitHub, and the organization’s team space.
Automated CI/CD scaffolding and troubleshot Azure Kubernetes clusters, Helm, and rollouts.
Co-maintained Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions pipelines with Docker and Kubernetes.
Supported Harbor and SonarQube deployments and operations on Kubernetes.
Created an ARM-based GitHub self-hosted runner and partnered on a migration from Azure DevOps to GitHub.
Resolved 1,000+ Level 2/3 incidents, wrote Python automation, and ran onboarding sessions twice monthly.
Assisted with CI/CD, deployments, monitoring checks, and production incident triage using Docker, Kubernetes, and Azure DevOps.
Advanced from Alpha to Beta milestone and conducted 15+ technical workshops on Java, web development, and cloud computing.
Completed hands-on Azure assignments and received the Best Mentor award.

projects.name: LogLens: AI-Powered Log Diagnosis & Learning
projects.description: A completed, language-agnostic log analysis tool for logs from any programming language or technology stack. LogLens identifies likely root causes, explains what went wrong, and provides practical solutions alongside relevant videos and links to help anyone understand and learn from the issue. It combines rule-based detection with a local Ollama LLM; logs stay on-device and secrets are redacted before analysis.
highlights: Analyzes logs across programming languages and technology stacks to identify likely root causes.
Explains what went wrong and provides practical solutions, relevant videos, and links for further learning.
Uses a local Ollama LLM and rule-based detection; redacts secrets and keeps logs on the user's machine.
